'''Gi Shatta Gasha''' was a [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] phrase of exultation and praise.

==History==
The words were shouted during the victory celebration over the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], news broke that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] had triumphed at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was confirmed dead, along with his right-hand man, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. In reaction to the news, uprisings and spontaneous celebrations broke out across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Several individuals were heard shouting this phrase during the [[Coruscant uprising|Coruscant Uprising]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}, 1997 Special Edition onwards.</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
For some time, it was rumored that the phrase being shouted at the ends of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] was "The [[Son of Suns/Legends|Son of Suns]]!", a phrase originating from some of the earliest [[Star Wars]] draft scripts as a prophetic quote from the [[Journal of the Whills/Legends|Journal of the Whills]] referencing the '[[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]]'. However, [[Matthew Wood]], supervising sound editor on the Star Wars prequel trilogy, established that the phrase that was shouted during both celebrations "was the result of Ben Burtt making up some Huttese language because, after all, not everyone in the Star Wars galaxy speaks Basic."<ref name="SWArchive-Debunking the Son of Suns Myth">{{SWArchive|url=movies/saga/20090204.html|text=Debunking the "Son of Suns" Myth}}</ref> However, the [[2013]] novel [[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy|''Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy'']] introduced another Huttese phrase, "[[Gi Dopa Gasha]]"&mdash;meaning "the two suns." This indicates that the Huttese word ''gasha'' does mean "sun."<ref name="DMSC">''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]''</ref>
